inconsistencies: Rebroadcast privacy cluster overlaps heavily: #36398 (rebroadcast only own txs), #36482 (only announce if re-added to mempool), #34533 (route rebroadcast through private broadcast), #36330 (suppress rebroadcast entirely under -privatebroadcast), #36380 (-walletbroadcast=initialonly) and #36481 (manual rebroadcast). Review #36398 first since it is the broadest fix; #34533 and #36330 are two mutually exclusive answers to the same -privatebroadcast leak and need one decision, not two reviews; #36481 is the user-facing escape hatch the restrictions create.

Multipath descriptor chain must be reviewed in order: #36442 (single Descriptor object) -> #36443 (reconstruct from expansion) -> #36444 (store in wallet DB). #36444 is useless until the first two land.
Multiprocess chain: #10102 depends on #29409 and is the prerequisite for #19460 (and #19461). #19460 has no standalone value before #10102.

Multisig-wizard (#35645) support PRs are fragmented across #36070 (deriveHDKey interface), #35918 (key expression parsing) and #36143 (CreateMultisigDescriptor); they should be assessed as one design, and #36126 (key labels) was NACKed on the same design area.
Silent payments: #32966 (receiving) and #35302 (sending, depends on #35301) are one project; receiving should be settled first.

Legacy-migration hardening is split across #34193 (rollback/staging), #36871 (BDB cursor stream reset), #36825 (watch-only migration failure), #35990 (BDB parser hardening) and #36823 (skip rather than erase records). They touch the same code paths and will conflict; #34193 restructures the flow and should go first.
#25722 (util::Result for wallet loading/creation/migration) rewrites the same signatures that #34193 and #34909 change; whichever lands first forces a rebase of the others.
PSBT signing/analysis fixes #36577, #35747, #36352 and #36039 all touch sign.cpp/FillPSBT paths; #36577 is the broadest and should be reviewed before the narrower ones.
#35998 (nodiscard on WalletBatch) and #34520 (nodiscard on bool+out-param getters) apply the same technique in overlapping files; coordinating them avoids duplicated churn.
Coin-selection test PRs #36614, #36732, #36740, #36840 and #36255 all edit coinselection_tests.cpp / coinselector_tests.cpp and will conflict with each other; batch them in one review pass.
result.notes: The band split is driven by the category's own priority order: fund safety and the legacy-to-descriptor migration path first, then privacy of transaction creation, then user-visible reliability, then features. P1 is reserved for the six PRs where leaving the problem unfixed means lost/corrupt wallet data, a load-time crash, a silently wrong balance, or a deanonymisation leak affecting every wallet user. P2 is wide (34 PRs) because this category genuinely has many durable privacy, correctness and migration improvements in flight; within it, certain bug fixes are ordered ahead of large but slower-landing feature projects. The long P3 tail is dominated by refactors and test coverage, which the rubric sinks unless the category is itself about internals.
